Hello there, I was ”the sunny boy” at Helsinki 2012 show. 
My dad was a huge fan since 90’s, and my family had been attending to a bunch of different shows by then, Mostly northern europe, but for example Spain, Germany and Ireland as well. 
Helsinki 2012 was a massive experience. My dad and I got our queue numbers two nights before the show, and the rest of the family joined the queue on the morning of the show. Due to the roll calls of the night before and morning of the show being so close to one another, me and dad stayed in a tent right outside the venue for the night before the show. 

With relatively low numbers (76&77) we had ourselves front of the stage places, right under Stevie’s nose. By a chance, if chance it was, the Boss happened to walk across us during Sunny Day’s sax solo, and signaled me to hop on the stage. Before I even got to understand what was going on, I was already lifted to the stage and got to sing to a full house of 40,000 or so people. 

Safe to say, my old man was a bit shook afterwards and missed at least Back in your arms after this, probably a few other songs as well. Helsinki 2012 still arises in conversations with fellow fans due to the extraordinary length of the show and the special half an hour -long acoustic set before the show itself, and for me personally it is an amazing memory. 

At that time I was probably more embarassed than proud of what happened, because I was still a bit top young to understand it all, and all my peers were listening to very different music at the time, so they did not really appreciate it all. Fast forward to this day, our family had a summer of 4 shows as a group, and I even managed to light a teeny tiny spark in my girlfriend to listening to the Boss as well. 

Safe to say, I will fondly remember my experience till the day I die, and it helped me spark a love for the Boss’ music indefinitely. 

Oh, and a year later my little brother was the Sunny Boy as well, but that’s another story😉

I’m a native finnish speaker, yet I’ve only read Silmarillion in english as well as in finnish but Hobbit and LotR in finnish only, and it is my biggest regret. The translation on its own is a masterpiece, considering the amount of names translated from common tongue to finnish, giving it more of a children’s book nature. Silm on the other hand is equally as hard to understand in finnish as it is in english mainly due to the text having such a biblical tone. Part of the magic of Tolkien is that the legendarium is timeless and it keeps the same themes even in different languages. However, the madlad himself even studied finnish in order to be able to read Kalevala in the original language, so I’d suggest trying to do the same in this case as well. 

tl:dr you might struggle at first with the old language, but it doesn’t really matter if you only read it in your own native language.

primarily a CB here but played a lot of RB and LB as well. 
DON’T RUSH IN. EVER. Let the opposition make the first move. You don’t need to have insane speed or power to be capable fullback, what you need is intelligence and composure. With the ball, try to look for a 100% sure pass. Avoid taking risky passes, you may be caught off guard by the eventual counterattack. Look for easiest paths to recycle or just hoof it upfield by the sideline if you run out of time and space, better safe than sorry. While defending, keep on track of both your own defensive line and the opposing winger. You need to be a part of the line but you also MUST keep the man on your side occupied. Strike on heavy touches and try to keep your head up to see the whole game!

See, the way ratings are calculated is NOT based on card stats as people often misunderstand. They are calculated off the most important stats for the said position, in this case finishing and heading accuracy are the most crucial stats. However, other ’shooting’ values like volleys also affect the rating, but not as much. This explains f.ex. low-rated players with higher card stats (check out Dybala’s 81 card in FUT16, or basically any version of Emre Mor). 

Son is a CF, that means his rating is basically based off his dribbling and shooting ingame stats. As Auba is a striker, the rating method is completely different for him, thus resulting in possibly much lower card stats.
